items.title: Morning Briefing: Oct. 31, 2026
items.excerpt: Merve Aydogan 31 October 2026• Update: 31 October 2026 HAMILTON, Canada Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start Saturday, including Polish President Karol Nawrocki aborting an Africa trip and returning to Warsaw as a power struggle erupts over control of the Constitutional Tribunal; Türkiye formally nominating OSCE Secretary-General Feridun Sinirlioglu as a candidate for UN secretary-general; and the US State Department approving a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 MSE missiles to Ukraine. Polish President Karol Nawrocki aborted a flight to Senegal and returned to Warsaw as rival groups of judges disputed control of the Constitutional Tribunal, after orders appeared on its website to temporarily remove its president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, and vice president Bartlomiej Sochanski, in a move the tribunal rejected as illegal and a "coup." Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska said she ordered the two to stop their duties, while police said they were deployed for possible threats to judges and had not entered the building. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said "restoring the rule of law is our duty," while opposition Law and Justice leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski called the events a "coup against the Constitutional Tribunal." Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski defended the police action as aimed at letting duly elected judges resume the court’s work, while US Ambassador Tom Rose urged restraint, calling the situation "very serious." ## Türkiye nominates OSCE chief Sinirlioglu as candidate for next UN secretary-general Türkiye formally nominated Feridun Sinirlioglu, secretary-general of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, as a candidate for UN secretary-general, after the latest Security Council straw poll ended inconclusively, according to Turkish Foreign Ministry sources. In a nomination letter transmitted by Türkiye's UN envoy Ahmet Yildiz to the presidents of the General Assembly and the Security Council, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan cited Sinirlioglu's more than 40 years in diplomacy, including as foreign minister and UN envoy, saying he possesses "the experience and culture of consensus required to lead the United Nations Organization." ## US approves $2.1B Patriot missile sale to Ukraine The US State Department approved a possible sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement missiles and related equipment to Ukraine at an estimated cost of $2.1 billion, saying the cost is "funded entirely by partners and allies" and that "no US funds are involved in this sale." Ukraine will pay with donations from Canada, Germany and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds financed by the EU’s Ukraine Support Loan, according to the agency, with Lockheed Martin as principal contractor. The approval comes days after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine has received an average of 12 Patriot interceptors per month from the US this year, while needing to intercept around 150 Russian ballistic missiles per month. ... ## Binance reports security incident, pledges to cover all user losses Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced it is managing a security incident, pledging to cover all user losses and saying it has reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds, including its Secure Asset Fund for Users, to protect customer balances, with $5 billion held in the exact impacted token assets. "Your funds are safe; Binance is covering the impact of this incident, not you," the exchange said in a statement.

items.title: While You Were Sleeping: 5 stories you might have missed, Oct 31, 2026 | The Straits Times
items.excerpt: ## ‘Anchor the ground’: Canada, EU launch new alliance The EU and Canada announced an alliance on Oct 30 aimed at cementing their own relations in the face of President Donald Trump’s moves to tear up US ties with its old partners. Canada agreed to contribute to a €90 billion (S$128 billion) support loan for Ukraine and work closer with Brussels on anything from critical minerals to artificial intelligence, after a two-day summit in Montreal. “The world’s becoming more dangerous and divided. Our societies are being shaken by new storms,” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told a press conference, mentioning eroding democratic norms and “the weaponisation of trade.” “Together, Canada and the European Union are anchoring the ground. Anchoring our ground to uphold our values while forming a protective canopy under which our citizens can all thrive,” he said, after talks with EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa. ## Nations agree push to get nature goals on track PHOTO: AFP Nearly 200 nations on Oct 30 adopted hard-fought agreements at a UN biodiversity summit aimed at putting the world back on track in efforts to halt nature’s destruction by 2030. Delegates cheered as the crucial texts were approved in overtime following two weeks of tense negotiations at the COP17 conference in Armenia’s capital Yerevan. “And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan to applause, as he brought down the gavel on the documents, the final versions of which were not immediately available. ## US midterm early voting hits record 48 million PHOTO: EPA A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week’s US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed Oct 30. The University of Florida’s Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022. The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s presidency.

items.title: PCE inflation report September 2026:
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 8:32 AM EDT Updated Thu, Oct 29 2026 2:06 PM EDT ... economy grew at a 3.4% pace in the third quarter, faster than expected. - Inflation continued to run above the Fed's 2% target in September, with a headline rate of 3.6% and core at 3.1%, according to the central bank's preferred gauge. ... The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below. Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends. While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter. Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%. The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move. "The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday. However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do. ... Economic growth has been driven by higher levels of investment from the artificial intelligence build-out, as well as high levels of consumer and government spending. Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products. Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter. There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter. September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%. At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

items.title: New economic data challenges Fed chief’s not-too-hot perspective By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - New data may challenge Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s sense that the US economy can handle a robust expansion without stoking inflation, as a key measure of price pressures jumped and strong consumer spending and business investment pushed growth further beyond the level most central bank officials see as sustainable. ... The pace may not continue. Consumer spending, for example, grew faster than income in the recent GDP report, a situation some economists said was unlikely to last, and Warsh said on Wednesday that a recent tightening in credit markets showed investors had become "more discerning in their capital allocations," a possible precursor to slower investment growth. But the data in hand still show an economy that so far has not slowed despite the outlook for tighter monetary policy, with strong demand now coinciding with broad-based inflation. Different measures of inflation’s breadth show anywhere from roughly 50% to nearly 60% of the items in the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, the gauge the Fed uses for its 2% inflation target, posting annual price increases of more than 3% in September — far above pre-COVID-19 norms for a measure Warsh said he sees as a good indicator of underlying inflation trends. Though the number of items above that 3% level fell slightly last month, Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG, said the details of the PCE report showed inflation was broadly persistent across the economy, particularly in service industries where Fed rate hikes may have less of an impact. The PCE Price Index rose 3.6% in September after a 3.4% rise in the previous month, pushing it further away from the recent low of 2.3% in March 2025, near the start of President Donald Trump’s second term in the White House.

items.title: 2026 elections live updates as Trump rallies Florida voters, El-Sayed clashes with Stevens
items.excerpt: Updated on: October 31, 2026 / 12:14 AM EDT / CBS News ## What to know as Election Day approaches for the 2026 midterms: - With just three days to go until Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3, candidates in key Senate and House elections are making their closing arguments to midterm voters. - President Trump held a rally in Florida, continuing a weekslong blitz. He reversed course and said he will hold rallies in Kansas and Ohio this weekend. - The DOJ pushed to segregate some Alaska Senate ballots, pending a probe into how a man with nearly the same name as GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan ended up on the ballot. Democrat Mary Peltola denied involvement. - A California judge late Friday issued a temporary restraining order directing the federal government to stop demanding that California state and local election officials separate out ballots or not count certain votes from alleged noncitizens. The judge also ordered the DOJ to stop threatening officials with criminal prosecution if they do not comply. - Democratic Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed clashed with former primary rival Haley Stevens. - The latest CBS News polling shows Democrats with an edge in the House — but the Senate could hinge on toss-up elections in Maine, Ohio, Texas and more. CBS News now rates South Carolina as a GOP-leaning battleground. ... ## Trump says he was asked to un-cancel rallies in Kansas and Iowa to "make sure that we win" During his rally in Florida late Friday, near the tail end of a weekslong campaign blitz, President Trump acknowledged that "28 days of this crap is a lot," telling the crowd his "voice is … operating at about 49.2%." "I thought this was going to be my last one," he said. "I thought this was it. I thought I could relax." Instead, Mr. Trump is planning to visit Iowa and Kansas on Sunday, two states with tight Senate races. He canceled his weekend rallies in both states on Thursday, but announced a day later that they're back on. He told the crowd in Daytona Beach that "they called me in Iowa and they called me in Kansas, and they said, 'Sir, would it be possible to do a little rally of about 50,000 people each?' And I said, 'Does it matter?' They said, 'We just want to make sure that we win.'" ... ## DOJ asks judge to segregate Alaska ballots listing Daniel J. Sullivan The Justice Department on Friday asked a federal judge to order Alaska officials to segregate all ballots that rank Daniel J. Sullivan, a Senate candidate with the same first and last name as the GOP incumbent. The filing came in a civil lawsuit from the Trump administration seeking to block the certification of Alaska's Senate election if Democrat Mary Peltola wins due to "voter confusion." Those efforts were amplified this week after The New York Times reported that operatives linked to Peltola's campaign helped recruit Daniel J. Sullivan — allegations Peltola has denied. Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward wrote Friday afternoon that "there is a substantial risk that Mr. Sullivan's sham candidacy will mislead voters and ultimately result in an electoral process that lacks integrity." For that reason, he argued, a preliminary injunction should be issued ordering Alaska to "preserve and segregate all ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan for the purposes of investigating whether such ranking was the product of voter confusion, should such an investigation become necessary." The federal government is also asking for expedited discovery into Peltola's campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Woodward asked a judge to rule by Monday. Alaska election officials opposed the request, arguing the Justice Department's lawsuit "lacks any merit." They also said votes are "comingled in the ballot box on Election Day" and therefore can't be segregated without violating ballot secrecy requirements, and noted that "the ballots (whether segregated or not) will not reveal any voter's reasons for voting for Daniel J." And they said an order to preserve ballots is unnecessary since the state already saves ballots for 22 months. "The United States' delay further undermines its request for expedited consideration. It waited until two weeks before Election Day to file a lawsuit about issues that arose months ago," the state said. The defendants in the case include Alaska Division of Elections Director Carol Beecher, who previously attempted to keep Daniel J. Sullivan off the ballot. ... ## In intra-party feud, El-Sayed says Stevens "seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago" Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate, hit back at Rep. Haley Stevens, whom he defeated in the primary, after she demanded an apology for comments he made about Israel. The dispute between the former Democratic rivals comes two days before they are expected to appear at an event in Detroit with Rep. James Clyburn of South Carolina — marking one of their only joint appearances since the contentious primary. In a statement Friday night, El-Sayed says his former rival "seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago" instead of focusing on beating the Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers and addressing Michiganders' cost of living concerns. Stevens said in an earlier statement Friday she planned to appear with El-Sayed on the campaign trail, but she expected him to apologize for comments about Israel and condemn an ad from an outside PAC that she said was antisemitic. She also wanted El-Sayed to take down his own ad featuring Tucker Carlson. "Abdul promises to get money out of politics," she said. items.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening election officials with criminal charges
items.excerpt: A federal judge issued a sweeping order Friday night blocking the Trump administration from threatening or intimidating election officials amid pressure tactics used by the administration in the weeks leading up to the Nov. 3 midterm elections. The eight-page order prohibits any action that may “threaten, intimidate or coerce state or local elections officials or workers to demand that they halt processing the ballots of any registered voter solely on the basis that the ballot belongs to an individual alleged by [the administration] to be ineligible to vote.” U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson, who’s based in California, wrote, “In the lead-up to the election, high-ranking DOJ and DHS officials have engaged in a campaign to intimidate, threaten, and coerce state and local officials and employees who are engaged in administering the ongoing midterm 2026 election.” The order comes in the wake of efforts to require states like California and Washington to separate out ballots the administration says could be cast by noncitizens. An appeals court ruled against the administration in California this week; the Washington case is pending. “Although Defendants claim that their actions are designed to halt unlawful voting by noncitizens, their actions are likely to have the effect of interfering with election administration and disenfranchising lawful voters,” Thompson wrote Friday. The judge’s order extends through Nov. 16, nearly two weeks after Election Day.

Stewart, knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II for his contributions to drama, died at his home in Los Angeles, according to a statement on his ‌X account. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, ​in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” ⁠it said. Meanwhile, Ian McKellen, who worked alongside Patrick in the X-Men films, took to Instagram and shared a photo of Patrick. He began his note by acknowledging that Patrick “was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire”. “You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love,” Ian said. >> Hundreds of applications exposed in censor board data breach A data breach at the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) exposed information from applications for more than 500 titles, dozens of which were feature films, The Hindu found. The leak appears to have originated from the e-Cinepramaan portal, launched nearly a decade ago to digitise the CBFC’s work. The exposed material includes detailed shooting scripts, cut orders and other documents submitted by filmmakers seeking certification for their films to be screened in Indian cinemas.
